title: HelperSSHPromptParams
description: The helper asking the coordinator's UI the questions a server's keyboard-interactive challenge carries (nocx-50w7p.11). It is the ONE reverse op whose subject is a PERSON rather than a stored secret: `secret` returns material the coordinator already holds, while this returns something nobody holds until the question is asked. The server's own prompts travel with it — their text and whether the answer is echoed — because that is what makes the ask answerable by somebody who is not looking at the far host, and because a question of nocx's own invention would leave a person answering something the server did not ask.

host.description: The host the question is about, as the RESOLVED value the destination carried. It is here so the ask can name the connection it belongs to: a bare 'enter password' box is how the wrong password ends up in the wrong connection.

port.description: The resolved port, for the same reason and by the same rule.

user.description: The resolved account the question names.

prompts.description: The server's questions, in the order it asked them. An empty list is refused rather than answered with nothing: a keyboard-interactive challenge with no questions is a protocol event with no question to relay.

prompt.description: The question's text, verbatim from the far side. It is passed through unchanged: the person answers the server, not nocx.

echo.description: Whether the answer is echoed. Load-bearing in a way that is easy to lose: a UI that does not know a question is secret would print the answer on a screen, and one that assumes every question is secret would hide a code the person has to read as they type it.
